H06 daily metrics — complete Stage 2 production

Complementary preregistration-oriented participant-day evidence and H06-D-G2 author gate

Published

August 12, 2026

1 Stage 2 verdict

ImportantH06-D-G2 status — author review required

The authorized production grid is complete: 468 non-L10 metric × predictor × scenario cells, 936 raw omnibus tests, 66,664 participant/site deletion refits, and 12 complete named 15-slot Benjamini–Hochberg (BH) families. L10 mean remains the frozen named non-estimable slot 3; MDER raw results remain frozen in slot 15, with only its mathematically dependent BH fields recalculated.

Of the 39 primary near-eye non-L10 cells, 4 are acceptable, 4 are acceptable only with an explicit limitation, and 31 do not support an unqualified association claim under the prespecified rules. The individual estimates and complete multiplicity vectors remain visible below so numerical results are not selected after diagnostics.

This document is the mandatory Stage 2 stop. It does not authorize the compact Stage 3 reader report, the separate Stage 4 provenance companion, website integration, or any change to the selected hourly main H06 analysis.

2 Scientific target and analysis roles

The daily variant asks how recorded day-level contexts are associated with participant-day light-exposure metrics. Each admissible metric-specific day contributes exactly one row. It neither models repeated hourly melEDI nor weights days by the number of supported hours. Under H06-007, the completed hourly H06 analysis remains the main analysis; this daily analysis is complementary evidence closer to the registered daily-metric outcome wording.

3 Exact production implementation

3.1 Model routes

The nine non-timing outcomes retain the approved fixed-site mixed-model hierarchy, with a participant random intercept:

response_value ~ site + (1 | participant_key)
response_value ~ site + predictor + (1 | participant_key)
response_value ~ site * predictor + (1 | participant_key)

Gaussian comparisons use maximum likelihood and estimates use REML. Tweedie models use a log link. The registered random-site/random-slope formula remains a visible benchmark and never replaces the fixed-site primary hierarchy.

The four repaired timing outcomes use the uniformly accepted fixed-site linear hierarchy:

response_value ~ site
response_value ~ site + predictor
response_value ~ site * predictor

Their covariance is participant-cluster HC3 from sandwich::vcovCL(type = "HC3", cadjust = TRUE, fix = FALSE), with participant-cluster-minus-one t/F references and pointwise 95% confidence intervals. No simultaneous interval is used.

Site uses sum-to-zero coding throughout. Categorical effects are Free day minus Work day and Active minus Sedentary. Sleep duration is the per-hour association for a previous-night duration centered at 8 h. Because this daily model does not include separate participant-mean and day-deviation sleep terms, that coefficient combines between-participant and within-participant comparisons; the participant random intercept does not by itself separate them. Equal-site marginalization is used rather than weighting sites by their number of observations.

4 Primary near-eye estimates

The two figures show adjusted effects and pointwise 95% confidence intervals. Ratios refer to the fitted response scale stated in the source table—for shifted-log outcomes, the ratio is for the fitted metric plus 0.1, not a raw metric ratio. Absolute timing and duration effects are shown in hours.

The paired source-data CSVs are sealed with the figures. The tables below give the exact samples, p-values, BH values, and diagnostic claim status behind the plots.

5.2 L10 and MDER dispositions

L10 mean melEDI remains NON_ESTIMABLE_COMPONENT_FAILURE in all 12 joint slots; its raw and adjusted p-values are missing. Positive-only and MAP results remain descriptive historical diagnostics and are not substituted. MDER uses the approved arithmetic mean of viable positive finite one-minute melEDI/illuminance ratios. Its raw model results are frozen; only family-wide adjusted fields change when the 15-slot vectors are completed.

The selected-candidate MDER point estimates and pointwise 95% intervals are retained below for context; they remain the sealed METRIC-010 results.

6 Complementary placement evidence

The placement comparisons below use the same approved model route within each metric. They are estimation-only: no additional p-value screen is created.

8.3 Temporal dependence and timing-route qualifications

The accepted timing route retains all earlier limitations. In particular, first timing above 250 lx melEDI for Work versus Free day had a 1.23-HC3-SE Student-t shift; L10 midpoint activity had a 1.26-HC3-SE no-nugget AR shift; three pilot additive AR fits were unresolved; no pilot AR structure met the pooled-and-every-site lag rule; and timing site interactions remain sensitivity-dependent. Production significance cannot erase these facts.

9 Comparison with V0

9.1 Implementation-level comparison

Component V0 implementation Current H06 daily implementation Claim consequence
Outcome Repeated hourly geometric-mean melEDI Fifteen distinct participant-day metrics Different estimands; no hourly coefficient transfers
Formula geo.MEDI ~ site*daytype + site*exercise + site*sleep_duration + (1|Id) Separate reduced/additive/site-interaction hierarchy for each metric and predictor No V0 coefficient maps one-to-one to a daily-metric result
Predictor encoding Free/work, four-level exercise intensity, and sleep duration jointly Work/Free day, day-level Active/Sedentary status, and within-person previous-night sleep duration separately Predictor meaning and adjustment differ
Day weighting One row per retained hour One row per admissible metric-specific participant-day Days are not weighted by supported-hour count
Dependence Participant intercept only Participant intercept or participant-cluster HC3, plus the prespecified actual-date temporal screen Uncertainty and diagnostic acceptance differ
Site Fixed interactions with a stale displayed site p-value Equal-site fixed-site association plus a separate heterogeneity test; registered benchmark visible Site evidence is reconstructed rather than copied
Multiplicity Raw predictor-block p-values labelled as FDR Twelve named 15-slot BH vectors V0 significance labels are not retained
Uncertainty Final table omitted 95% intervals Pointwise 95% intervals for every estimable effect Magnitude and uncertainty are explicit
Placement Signed chest primary but near-eye-focused reporting Near eye primary; chest and paired/common complementary Placement roles are transparent

9.2 Claim-level disposition

V0 hourly ratios, site contrasts, and “unique variance” fractions remain historical descriptors. They cannot be restated as effects on daily mean, M10/L10, threshold durations, exposure timing, melEDI dose, MDER, or the longest continuous period. This Stage 2 analysis supports only metric-specific observational statements on its own exact frames and only where the declared diagnostic status permits them. Numerical similarity between hourly and daily results is neither expected nor an equivalence test.

10 Reproducibility and runtime

The input manifest contains 34 sealed identities; the scientific-output manifest contains 987 identities; the figure manifest pairs two publication-scale figures with two source-data CSVs; and the final preservation audit confirms 634 protected historical H06_daily and main-H06 files byte-for-byte.

The current prepared metrics retain the PREP06-BASE-002 qualification: state-support reconstruction inherits the bounded PREP-003/FIND-044 provenance limitation. This qualification is not evidence that the current metric values are analytically wrong.

11 H06-D-G2 author decisions

ImportantStop gate — explicit Stage 2 approval required

Please approve or amend all of the following before any Stage 3 work:

  1. Accept the completed 468-cell production grid, exact samples, model routes, and pointwise 95% intervals as the Stage 2 implementation record.
  2. Accept the twelve complete named 15-slot BH families, with L10 retained as the frozen NA slot and MDER raw/model outputs frozen.
  3. Accept the explicit cell-level diagnostic verdicts, including every not-acceptable result and major limitation; no small p-value overrides a failed diagnostic.
  4. Accept the chest, paired/common, and gap-timing-unaware results in their declared complementary or sensitivity roles.
  5. Retain the completed hourly H06 analysis as the main H06 result and this daily analysis as complementary preregistration-oriented evidence.
  6. Decide separately whether to authorize Stage 3: a compact standalone reader-facing notebooks/hypotheses/H06_daily.qmd. Stage 4 remains blocked until that Stage 3 report is itself approved.

No model refit, deletion batch, multiplicity change, Stage 3/4 authoring, website integration, shared edit, main-H06 change, commit, or push follows automatically from this gate.

find_project_root <- function(start = getwd()) {
  candidate <- normalizePath(start, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
  repeat {
    if (file.exists(file.path(candidate, "renv.lock"))) return(candidate)
    parent <- dirname(candidate)
    if (identical(parent, candidate)) {
      stop("Could not locate the project root", call. = FALSE)
    }
    candidate <- parent
  }
}

artifact <- function(stage, file) {

read_h06d <- function(stage, file) {
  readr::read_csv(

sha256 <- function(path) digest::digest(path, algo = "sha256", file = TRUE)
verify_relative_manifest <- function(manifest, hash_column = "sha256") {
  paths <- file.path(project_root, manifest$relative_path)
  stopifnot(all(file.exists(paths)))
  actual <- unname(vapply(paths, sha256, character(1)))
  stopifnot(identical(actual, manifest[[hash_column]]))
  invisible(TRUE)
}
compact_gt <- function(table, source_note = NULL) {
  output <- table |>
    gt::gt() |>
    gt::tab_options(
      table.font.size = gt::px(12),
      data_row.padding = gt::px(3),
      heading.padding = gt::px(4),
      column_labels.padding = gt::px(4),
      table.width = gt::pct(100),
      source_notes.font.size = gt::px(11),
      row_group.padding = gt::px(4)
    )
  if (!is.null(source_note)) {
    output <- output |> gt::tab_source_note(gt::md(source_note))
  }
  output
}
format_p <- function(value) {
  dplyr::case_when(
    is.na(value) ~ "—",
    value < 0.001 ~ "<0.001",
    TRUE ~ sprintf("%.3f", value)
  )
}
`%||%` <- function(x, y) if (length(x) == 0L || is.na(x)) y else x
format_effect <- function(estimate, lower, upper, scale) {
  digits <- ifelse(grepl("^ratio", scale), 3L, 2L)
  ifelse(
    is.na(estimate),
    "—",
    sprintf(
      paste0("%.", digits, "f (%.", digits, "f to %.", digits, "f)"),
      estimate,
      lower,
      upper
    )
  )
}
short_status <- function(value) {
  dplyr::recode(
    value,
    ACCEPTABLE = "Acceptable",
    ACCEPTABLE_WITH_LIMITATION = "Acceptable with limitation",
    NOT_ACCEPTABLE = "Not acceptable",
    .default = value
  )
}

## L10 and MDER dispositions

L10 mean melEDI remains `NON_ESTIMABLE_COMPONENT_FAILURE` in all 12 joint
slots; its raw and adjusted p-values are missing. Positive-only and MAP results
remain descriptive historical diagnostics and are not substituted. MDER uses
the approved arithmetic mean of viable positive finite one-minute
melEDI/illuminance ratios. Its raw model results are frozen; only family-wide
adjusted fields change when the 15-slot vectors are completed.

## Temporal dependence and timing-route qualifications

The accepted timing route retains all earlier limitations. In particular,
first timing above 250 lx melEDI for Work versus Free day had a 1.23-HC3-SE
Student-t shift; L10 midpoint activity had a 1.26-HC3-SE no-nugget AR shift;
three pilot additive AR fits were unresolved; no pilot AR structure met the
pooled-and-every-site lag rule; and timing site interactions remain
sensitivity-dependent. Production significance cannot erase these facts.

# Comparison with V0

## Implementation-level comparison

| Component | V0 implementation | Current H06 daily implementation | Claim consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Outcome | Repeated hourly geometric-mean melEDI | Fifteen distinct participant-day metrics | Different estimands; no hourly coefficient transfers |
| Formula | `geo.MEDI ~ site*daytype + site*exercise + site*sleep_duration + (1|Id)` | Separate reduced/additive/site-interaction hierarchy for each metric and predictor | No V0 coefficient maps one-to-one to a daily-metric result |
| Predictor encoding | Free/work, four-level exercise intensity, and sleep duration jointly | Work/Free day, day-level Active/Sedentary status, and within-person previous-night sleep duration separately | Predictor meaning and adjustment differ |
| Day weighting | One row per retained hour | One row per admissible metric-specific participant-day | Days are not weighted by supported-hour count |
| Dependence | Participant intercept only | Participant intercept or participant-cluster HC3, plus the prespecified actual-date temporal screen | Uncertainty and diagnostic acceptance differ |
| Site | Fixed interactions with a stale displayed site p-value | Equal-site fixed-site association plus a separate heterogeneity test; registered benchmark visible | Site evidence is reconstructed rather than copied |
| Multiplicity | Raw predictor-block p-values labelled as FDR | Twelve named 15-slot BH vectors | V0 significance labels are not retained |
| Uncertainty | Final table omitted 95% intervals | Pointwise 95% intervals for every estimable effect | Magnitude and uncertainty are explicit |
| Placement | Signed chest primary but near-eye-focused reporting | Near eye primary; chest and paired/common complementary | Placement roles are transparent |

## Claim-level disposition

V0 hourly ratios, site contrasts, and “unique variance” fractions remain
historical descriptors. They cannot be restated as effects on daily mean,
M10/L10, threshold durations, exposure timing, melEDI dose, MDER, or the
longest continuous period. This Stage 2 analysis supports only metric-specific
observational statements on its own exact frames and only where the declared
diagnostic status permits them. Numerical similarity between hourly and daily
results is neither expected nor an equivalence test.
